newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-INTER GO DOWN 1-0 AT MONACO BUT REACH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER GO DOWN 1-0 AT MONACO BUT REACH FINAL.

text.p: Internazionale reached their third UEFA Cup final of the decade despite going down 1-0 to Monaco in the second leg of their semifinal on Tuesday, qualifing 3-2 on aggregate.
The Italian side, winners in 1991 and 1994, meet Schalke of Germany, who eliminated Spain's Tenerife 2-1 on aggregate, in the two-leg final next month.
Nigerian striker Victor Ikpeba, who scored Monaco's only goal in a 3-1 first leg defeat in Milan, gave the French league leaders new hope when he volleyed home in the 70th minute.
Inter claimed handball but the referee patted the right side of his chest, showing midfielder Sylvain Legwinski had controlled the ball legally as he laid on the goal.
The Italians weathered a Monaco storm after tricky teenage winger Thierry Henry came on for Scotland's John Collins with less than half an hour to go.
Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson said: "Monaco had a great match, the Inter defence was severely tested. We had a few chances to score in the first half but when you miss it becomes very tough.
"It's great to reach the final, but that was a hard way to do it."
With the home side committed to attack, Inter came as close as the width of a post to equalising in the final minutes.
First striker Maurizio Ganz, who scored twice in the first leg, broke through and looked set to score but central defender Martin Djetou just got back in time to boot the ball over for a corner.
Two minutes from time, substitute Marco Banca hit Monaco keeper Fabien Barthez's near post after breaking through on the right.
Monaco twice earlier in the match had the ball in the Italian net only to have the efforts disallowed.
Djetou's early headed effort was ruled out for a foul in a packed six-yard box while Henry had a goal disallowed for offside.

Monaco coach Jean Tigana said afterwards: "One fights against elements against which you can't defend yourself. I can't see why the first goal was disallowed... Now we must concentrate on winning the (French) championship."
Olympic gold medal winner Ikpeba said: "We've missed out on the final because of one poor half in Milan. It's a pity."

The Italian side's former Monaco forward Youri Djorkaeff said: "We came up against a great Monaco. If they had played like that in the first leg it would have been different. We ran, we defended. Tactically, we were strong."
In the 11th minute, left-back Lilian Martin hit a scorching 30-metre drive that took Gianluca Pagliuca by surprise and the Inter keeper barely managed to turn the ball over for a corner.
Pagliuca also made a diving save from a header by Legwinski at a corner and Monaco's tireless midfelder Emmanuel Petit blasted the rebound just over the bar.
At the other end, Barthez had to come out smartly to smother the ball as Inter's two Frenchmen Jocelyn Angloma and Djorkaeff combined on a dangerous run through the middle of the Monaco defence.
The match was Inter captain Giuseppe Bergomi's 97th in European competition, equalling the record of legendary Real Madrid winger Francisco Gento.
